newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs to sell 66 pct of biggest power plant.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs to sell 66 pct of biggest power plant.

text.p: Kazakhstan will hold a tender on July 21 for the right to own a 66 percent stake in the country's largest thermal power plant, AO Ekibastuzskaya GRES-2, in the northern Pavlodar region, the government announced on Monday.

The finance ministry's privatisation department said the stake being tendered is worth 16.875 billion tenge ($223.5 million), and tender conditions called for a minimum investment of 29.9 billion tenge ($387 million) by 2002.
"The price paid by a winner may be less than $223.5 million but its investment offer would have to be the best," a privatisation official told Reuters.

Foreign investors will not be barred from the auction. "The winner of the tender will be the participant who offers the most efficient economic programme and the highest price for the unit," an official report said.

The current capacity of the two energy blocks of the plant which is wholly owned by the state is 1,000 megawatts but would double after the launch of two blocks envisaged by the official investment project.

The report said the total investment needed includes no less than 20.2 billion tenge ($267.6 million) to be spent on the completion of the plant's construction and another nine billion ($119.2 million) on repair work by 2002.
Investors must also propose measures to improve the social protection of the plant's workers and pay off its debts to creditors.
